title: How to add a business line to your cell phone: VoIP, carrier, and eSIM
summary: Learn about three ways to add a business line to the cell phone you already own and how much each costs. Find out how a VoIP app compares to a carrier second line.
body_markdown:

You can’t ignore it, but you really wish there were a better way.


Using your[personal phone number to take business calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/using-your-personal-phone-number-for-business-heres-why-you-shouldnt/) is never ideal if you want privacy and a work-life balance. But[carrying around two mobile phones](https://www.quo.com/blog/carrying-two-phones/) ? That doesn’t make sense either.


So, can you add a business line to your cell phone? Yes, in three different ways:


1. **A VoIP app** gives you access to business numbers inside a dedicated app. They’re easy to set up and cost-effective for teams.
2. **A carrier second line** adds a cellular number to your existing account for roughly $10 to $15 a month. However, it needs a phone with a free eSIM slot. Providers like Verizon offer it as an add-on to your existing phone plan.
3. **Dual SIM phones** are another option for you to[add two phone numbers to a single device](https://www.quo.com/blog/2-phone-numbers-on-1-phone/) . You can get a second phone number with your existing carrier or a different carrier. Add numbers with a physical SIM or an eSIM.


VoIP phone services are often the best option for fast-growing teams. All it takes is finding the[right VoIP phone service](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-service/) ,[getting a business phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/) , and inviting your teammates to get started. But if you’re a solopreneur who needs a second phone number, you might be better off getting an additional number with your carrier.


Keep reading to learn what questions you need to ask before choosing a business line. Find out how to set up a business line, and why having a second number on your[VoIP cell phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-cell-phone/) is beneficial.


Luckily, you don’t need a second bulky device to separate business from personal — you can have[two phone numbers on a single device](https://www.quo.com/blog/2-phone-numbers-on-1-phone/) . Adding a business line to your cell phone is all about finding the[right VoIP phone service](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-service/) .

##


3 ways to add a business line to your cell phone


Here’s a breakdown of each of the methods you can use to get a second phone number:


### **1. VoIP apps**


Voice over Internet Protocol, or VoIP for short, apps make calls and send texts using an internet connection. They manage virtual phone numbers that aren’t tied to a specific device. They also offer more business-friendly features than carrier-provided numbers. You can share numbers with your teammates, automatically log calls in a CRM, and even have AI agents take calls for you.


VoIP providers like Quo make it easy to get a business phone number in minutes. Simply install their app, pick a business phone number, and invite your team. No SIM and no carrier involvement needed. Another advantage of using VoIP apps is that you can access your VoIP number across devices. That includes your laptop, tablet, and computer.


However, VoIP apps have one downside you should keep in mind as you consider adding a business line to your cell phone. They can’t accept mobile phone verification codes. Since they’re so easy to acquire and use, institutions like banks, ride-hailing apps, and government entities don’t accept them for verifying your identity in their systems. As telephony infrastructure provider[Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/best-practices/fraud-prevention-twilio-account-security) mentions: “ *As with account signup, users with multiple accounts and VOIP numbers are potential signals of fraudulent intent.”*


### **2. Carrier second line**


Major carriers sell a packaged second number as an add-on to your existing account. This is a phone number tied to their cellular networks. To get access to this second number, you need a cell phone with dual SIM or eSIM capabilities. While these phone numbers can accept verification codes for you, they come with several limitations you should know:


- **No shared numbers.** You can’t share these numbers with your team, unless you physically hand over your device to a colleague.
- **Single device only.** A carrier-provided second number lives in your cell phone. You can’t access it on your computer or on another phone.
- **No additional business phone features.** These types of numbers are limited to what they can do on your phone. They don’t have CRM syncing, automatic call summaries and transcripts, or automated texting features.


Examples of these second lines include[Verizon Second Number](https://www.quo.com/blog/verizon-second-number-alternatives/) , which is available as an add-on to your existing plan at $10 to $15 per number per month. Similarly, AT&T, and T-Mobile offer additional lines in their existing plans.


### **3. Dual SIM phones**


A dual SIM phone is a mobile device that has the option for two SIM cards. Each SIM card connects to its respective mobile network; you can choose to make calls from your second SIM card. It’s also convenient if you’re traveling and need to quickly get a local SIM in your destination country.


This is essentially the same method as getting a carrier-provided second line. The difference is you manually acquire your second SIM instead of buying it directly from your existing carrier. You might choose this approach to combine SIMs from multiple providers to increase your chances of always having a signal to make calls.


Just like carrier-provided second lines, dual SIM phones also fall short for business use. They’re locked to an individual device, so your team can’t access it easily. Plus, setup time can take hours if you have to purchase a new SIM from your carrier.

Most VoIP providers support local numbers, which have area codes tied to specific locations, like 206 for Seattle or 602 for Phoenix. A[local number](https://www.quo.com/local-numbers) can help you build trust with clients in a specific area, the same way you might be more likely to take a call from a neighbor than a stranger across the country.


If you’re doing business across North America, a[toll-free number](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers) can be a great alternative to local numbers. They make your business appear more established to your customers. They also allow callers from over 20 North American countries and territories to dial your number for free.

##


****Frequently asked questions about adding a business line to your cell phone****


**What type of phone do I need to add a business line?**


Any smartphone running iOS 14+ or Android 8+ works with VoIP apps like Quo. You don’t need any special hardware to use a VoIP app. Dual-SIM phones let you get a second business line through cellular plans. Any iPhone XS or newer and any current Android flagship can accommodate multiple SIMs.


**What happens to my business line when I upgrade my phone?**


VoIP numbers stay with your account, not device. All you need to do is download the VoIP app on your new phone and sign in — all history, contacts, and settings transfer. You won’t need to port your number since this is only required when switching your number between carriers, not devices.


**What’s the difference between adding a business line to an iPhone versus an Android?**


With VoIP apps, there’s no difference between iOS and Android. They operate identically on both platforms. When you’re adding a business line using dual SIM or eSIM, iPhones and Androids offer different methods to add a second phone number. Different models on each platform have their own settings to keep in mind.


**How long does it take to port my existing business number to my cell phone?**


[Number porting](https://support.quo.com/getting-started/porting/overview) typically takes between 5-10 business days. You’ll need your account number, PIN, and billing info from your current carrier to start the process. If your number is under an active contract, you may need to pay an early termination fee before porting.


**What’s the difference between a business line and a second number?**


There’s not much difference between the terms. They’re often used interchangeably. Both refer to a dedicated number separate from your personal line. The main difference is how you get it: a VoIP app gives you a second number or business line instantly on your existing device, a carrier second line adds one through your mobile plan, and dual-SIM lets you run two carrier lines on one phone.


**Can I use my business line on multiple devices at the same time?**


Yes. With Quo, you can access your business number on your phone, computer, and browser simultaneously. Calls and texts sync across all devices in real time, so you won’t miss anything whether you’re at your desk or on the go.


****Does my business number need to match the area code where I am located?****


No it doesn’t. You can get a business number outside your location’s area code with a VoIP app. However, your customers might recognize a local area code depending on the type of business you operate. You’ll be able to build trust and familiarity faster with a local area code.


****What are the benefits of getting a business number on my existing cell phone vs. carrying two phones?****


If you need to make the case to your boss to go from carrying two phones to adding a virtual number on your existing phone, a few reasons that’ll convince them to make the switch are:


– Team members can collaborate and solve customer problems together with[shared numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) that let them access entire customer conversation histories.
– You can access automation features that help you save time, like auto-replies and scheduled texts.
– Get set up and running with your new business phone number within minutes since you don’t need to buy additional equipment for each team member.
– Team members can work from anywhere around the world without having to worry about expensive international calling and texting rates.


**How much does it cost to add a business line to a cell phone?**


It depends on how you get one. VoIP services typically run $10–$30 per user per month — Quo starts at $15 — and includes features like call forwarding, AI insights, and integrations. Carrier second lines can be cheaper at $10–$15 per month but come with limited business features. Dual-SIM requires a compatible phone which can cost $300–$1,000, plus an extra monthly fee for the line itself.


Free options like Google Voice exist but have limited business features and mostly non-existent support.


**Is a business phone line tax deductible?**


Generally, yes. The IRS allows you to deduct the business-use percentage of your phone bill, and a VoIP subscription is usually fully deductible as a business software expense. Track your usage and hold onto records.
If you want more information, see IRS documentation on[home office and phone deduction rules](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p587) . Your tax professional can also help you calculate the right deduction for your situation.


**Can clients tell I’m using a VoIP business line?**


No, to your clients, calls look and sound like any other phone call. Your business number and name shows up on their[caller ID](https://www.quo.com/blog/business-caller-id/) , like a traditional number would. Call quality over 4G, 5G, or a strong WiFi connection matches carrier quality in most areas. The only time quality can dip is on a weak or unstable connection, so it’s worth making a few test calls before you start using your number with clients.


**What is the best phone service for a small business?**


The best VoIP service depends on your business needs. Quo is a great option for startups and small teams, while providers like RingCentral, Dialpad, and Grasshopper offer different features and pricing that may suit enterprise companies.


**What happens to my business number if I cancel my VoIP service?**


You can port your number out to another carrier before canceling, so you don’t lose it. Under FCC regulations, you have the right to transfer your number between providers. If you cancel without porting first, the number is typically released and may become available to someone else, so it’s worth initiating a port before you close your account.
